ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows passages separated by multiple black-bordered rectangular obstacles. A is located in a position somewhat to the lower right in the image, in the narrow vertical passage on the right side of the central vertical rectangular obstacle, and the arrow shows that Nick initially faces upward. B is located in an open passage in the upper left near the left boundary. There is a relatively long horizontal rectangular obstacle above, there is also a long horizontal rectangular obstacle somewhat to the right at the bottom, and there are passable outer passages along both the right and left edges. Reasoning: First give a route that only needs 4 right turns: from A, first go straight upward according to the arrow direction; turn right to the east at the upper passage; after reaching the right outer passage, turn right to the south; after reaching the lower passage, turn right to the west, and go around along the bottom passage to the left side; then turn right to the north, and go along the left passage to reach B. Therefore 4 right turns are sufficient. Then explain that fewer than 4 times is not enough. Nick initially faces north and can only turn right, so if at most 3 right turns are allowed, the possible direction sequences can only be N, N-E, N-E-S, or N-E-S-W. The first three ultimately still cannot reach B in the upper left, because the route cannot turn toward the left outer passage. If there are exactly 3 right turns, the last segment must go west to reach the height of B; but the vertical passage starting from A toward the north will be blocked by the upper horizontal rectangular obstacle before reaching the height where B is located, so it cannot form a route entering B westward at the height of B. Therefore 3 times or fewer is impossible. At least 4 right turns are needed.

raw_record.question_text: Nick can turn right but not left on his bicycle. What is the least number of right turns he must make in order to get from $A$ to $B$?

method.method_draft: Model the picture as corridors around the rectangular blocks. From the image, note that Nick starts at A facing upward in the narrow vertical passage just right of the central vertical block, and B is in the open left margin near the top-left. Exhibit a 4-right-turn path: go straight up from A through the vertical passage; make a right turn east through the horizontal gap below the top long block; make a right turn south down the open right-side margin; make a right turn west along the open bottom corridor below the bottom long block; then make a right turn north up the open left margin to B. To prove fewer do not work, enumerate the possible heading sequences with at most 3 right turns: N, N-E, N-E-S, or N-E-S-W. The first three cannot reach the left side where B lies. With exactly three turns, the final westward segment would need to be at B's height, but the initial northward segment from A is blocked by the top horizontal rectangle before reaching that height, so such a westward approach to B is impossible. Therefore the minimum is 4.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是由多个黑边矩形障碍物隔出的通道。A 位于图中偏右下的位置，在中央竖直矩形障碍物的右侧窄竖通道中，箭头显示 Nick 起始面向上方。B 位于左上方靠近左边界的开放通道中。上方有一条较长的水平矩形障碍物，底部偏右也有一条长水平矩形障碍物，右侧和左侧边缘都有可通行的外侧通道。

推理：先给出一条只需 4 次右转的路线：从 A 按箭头方向先一直向上；在上方通道处右转向东；到右侧外侧通道后右转向南；到下方通道后右转向西，沿底部通道绕到左侧；再右转向北，沿左侧通道到达 B。因此 4 次右转足够。

再说明少于 4 次不够。Nick 初始面向北，只能右转，所以若最多 3 次右转，可能的方向序列只能是 N，N-E，N-E-S，或 N-E-S-W。前三种最终仍不能到达左上方的 B，因为路线无法转向左侧外通道。若正好 3 次右转，最后一段必须向西到达 B 的高度；但从 A 起始向北的竖直通道在到达 B 所在高度之前会被上方水平矩形障碍物阻挡，不能形成在 B 高度向西进入 B 的路线。因此 3 次或更少不可能。最少需要 4 次右转。
